# Harness JSON format v1

Normative technical contract; Python 3.10+ standard library only. Machine documents use JSON, UTF-8, unique keys, unknown fields rejected. All decoded JSON keys and string values must contain Unicode scalar values; isolated surrogate escapes are rejected as `E_UNICODE` before schema/path processing (exit 1). Normal Chinese, emoji and correctly paired surrogate escapes are accepted. No manifest command is executed. The bundled schemas use a declared Draft 2020-12 subset: `$schema`, `$id`, `title`, `description`, `type` (object/array/string/integer/boolean/null, including type arrays), `properties`, `required`, `additionalProperties` (boolean or schema), `items`, `minItems`, `uniqueItems`, `minLength`, `pattern`, `enum`, `const`, `minimum`. The checker inspects the entire schema tree, including absent properties and empty-array item schemas, and rejects unsupported keywords/types. It is not a general JSON Schema validator. All supplied schema shapes use only this subset; semantic checks below are intentionally additional. Paths are root-relative POSIX paths; absolute, backslash, drive, traversal and escaping symlink references are rejected. Existing product directories need not move.

## Files and CLI

`tools/harness.py --help`
`python tools/harness.py lint --root examples/demo --manifest harness.json`
`python tools/harness.py resolve --root examples/demo --manifest harness.json --task tasks/hybrid.json`
`python tools/harness.py evidence --root examples/demo --manifest harness.json --task tasks/hybrid.json --records evidence/records.json --now 2026-11-14T10:00:00Z`

All outputs except argparse help are JSON, with `schema_version: 1`, `status`, `errors` (objects `code`, `path`, `message`) and command-specific fields. Exit 0 = valid/complete for requested operation (N/A allowed with scope proof); 1 = invalid input/schema/reference; 2 = unresolved/blocked/fail/not-run current checks; 3 = I/O or unexpected operational error. CLI misuse exits 2 via argparse. Lint success proves structure/references only, never execution or authorization.

## Manifest (`harness.json`, arbitrary filename accepted)

Required top-level: `schema_version` (=1), `project_id`, `owners`, `executors`, `rules`, `routes`. Optional: none. Every collection is an array; IDs unique within each kind. Owners: `{id, contact, backup}`. Executors: `{id, version, kind}` where kind is `manual|automated|schema`; these are identities, not executable commands. Rules: `{id, revision, owner, scope, source, statement, enforcement, executor_refs, evidence_refs, constraints}`. Enforcement is `proposed|advisory|enforced`, independent of result states. Scope: `{actions, paths, platforms, tasks, lifecycle, exclusions}` arrays of nonempty strings; `*` matches any dimension, paths use glob semantics below. Rule revisions positive integers. `source` is an existing page. `constraints` is an array of `{key, value}`; simultaneous applicable values differing for the same key stop affected actions across scopes. Keys are project-defined semantic constraint IDs; prose conflicts still require human review. `evidence_refs` names required check IDs.

Routes: `{id, owner, match, context_set, rule_refs, executor_refs, evidence_refs}`. Match: `{tasks, paths, platforms, domains, effects, mode}`; mode `all|task-or-path`. Empty arrays disable a dimension; nonempty dimensions require intersection; `*` universal. In task-or-path mode task/path are ORed, other dimensions are ANDed. Context: `{required, conditional}` with required page paths and conditional array `{when, add}`. `when` is `{fact, equals}` where equals is boolean. Missing or null fact is UNKNOWN and blocks, not false/N/A. Multiple matched routes union all pages/rules/executors/check IDs. Every declared rule must be referenced by a route; each task must match at least one route. Nonmatching routes are valid, listed as unmatched; zero routes or orphan rules fail lint. Every rule executor/check must appear in each referencing route; extra route executor/check IDs not owned by its referenced rules are rejected (`E_ORPHAN_EXECUTOR`/`E_ORPHAN_CHECK`). Required checks are derived only from applicable rules, not all matched route metadata. Within a rule, values of one dimension are ORed and separate dimensions are ANDed. Every supplied task/path/platform/domain/effect must be covered by at least one matched route, otherwise resolve blocks with `E_UNCOVERED_DIMENSION`. For task-or-path mode, task/path coverage is symmetric OR: a nonempty matching task selector covers supplied paths, and a nonempty matching path selector covers supplied tasks. Platforms/domains/effects still require independent coverage for every supplied value; the task/path OR never bypasses these dimensions. All task actions stop on unknown conditions/uncovered or unauthorized scope; explicit conflicts stop only their intersecting actions.

## Task (resolve/evidence input)

`{schema_version, change_id, tasks, paths, platforms, domains, effects, actions, lifecycle, facts, approved_paths, source, environment, target, artifacts}`. Arrays contain unique strings. Facts map names to boolean or null. `source`: `{base_commit, commit, dirty_digest}`. Environment: `{os, arch, shell, toolchain_digest, config_digest, permissions_digest, dependencies_digest}`. Target: `{kind, id, version, simulated}`; exact concrete target identity required, not latest/local/unknown. Artifacts array `{path, sha256}`; referenced regular files must exist within root and SHA-256 must match. Source commits are nonempty opaque identifiers, SHA digests 64 lowercase hex. Approved paths are explicit authorization input, never granted by tool; changes outside them block affected actions. Task paths match rules/globs case-sensitively on every OS. Lifecycle and actions determine scoped rules.

Path globs: `*` and `?` within one segment; `**` whole segment matches zero or more segments. No negation or brace expansion. Square brackets are literal filename characters, not character classes; non-pattern file references reject only `*` and `?` wildcards. Paths use `/`; a trailing slash is invalid. Re-run resolve whenever task identity/dimensions/paths/facts/source/environment/target/artifacts change. Output includes a deterministic `routing_digest` and `reroute_on` hints. The digest is SHA-256 of UTF-8 JSON (`sort_keys=True`, compact separators, ensure_ascii=False) over `{manifest, task, context_digests}`, where context_digests maps every declared source/required/conditional page to its content SHA-256. Array order is significant (safe conservative invalidation); object key order is not. Records must carry this exact digest; task dimensions/facts/path or document/manifest changes invalidate old evidence with `routing-changed`. All record invalidation_triggers must additionally include `routing`. Resolve is read-only and trusts supplied source/environment/target/approved_paths declarations; it does not inspect Git or authenticate authorization. The tool reads declared state, not Git or actual OS configuration.

## Evidence bundle

`{schema_version, records}` with each record `{id, change_id, rule_id, rule_revision, check_id, executor_id, executor_version, status, scope, routing_digest, source, environment, target, artifacts, collected_at, valid_until, invalidation_triggers, execution, na_basis, limitations}`. `status` exactly `pass|fail|blocked|not-run|not-applicable`. Scope is the rule scope structure. Source/environment/target/artifacts use task structures. RFC3339 timestamps must include timezone; validity finite and ordered. Invalidation triggers MUST include `source`, `environment`, `target`, `artifacts`, `rule`, `executor`, `scope`, `change`, `routing`. Execution: `{performed, command, cwd, exit_code, observation}`; command is descriptive string, never executed; exit_code integer or null. N/A basis is null or `{reason, scope_dimension, excluded_values}` where dimension is tasks/paths/platforms/actions/lifecycle and exclusions must demonstrate rule does not apply to current task; unknown capability is not N/A. Limitations is string array.

Pass requires performed=true, exit_code=0, nonempty command/observation, artifacts, executor kind not schema, and nonsimulated target. Evidence must bind all current state exactly, rule revision, executor version and scope; times must include now. Artifact bytes are checked. Stale historical statuses remain unchanged, current_status becomes not-run with invalidation_reasons. Missing required records become not-run; unresolved conditions/scope conflicts yield blocked. Proposed/advisory do not become enforced due to pass. Duplicate record IDs and duplicate (rule_id,check_id) pairs are rejected; unknown refs fail. Required checks derive from applicable rules of matched routes. N/A for applicable rule is rejected; absent/unscoped checks never imply pass.

Aggregate precedence: fail > blocked > not-run > pass; all N/A => not-applicable; zero applicable checks => not-applicable with resolved scope basis. An invalid current pass never counts. This is offline consistency validation, not signature verification, product acceptance, external protection enforcement, or permission authorization. Explicit schema files cover exactly the shapes above; custom cross-reference/scope/digest/freshness checks are additional normative semantics.
